sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Vertigo : tendency to fall to left side. Head-
ache: coniusion in head on rising suddenly. Incipient
tonza. Piercing pain in temples.

sections.label: Eyes
sections.text:
Retinal hamorrhage. Retinitis after in-
fluenza, also albuminuric.

sections.label: Ears
sections.text:
Roaring and ringing in cars. Deafness, with
vertigo.

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Sore, red and swollen. Pharyngitis ; swal-
lowing difficult.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Canker sores, with burning soreness and
fetid breath. Flatulence; hoi, sour belching. Putrid
fermentation. Fermentative dyspepsia. Tongue pur-
plish, leaden-colored.

Stools. — Putrid diarrhoea ; stools like green frog’s
spawn. [Magn. carh.]

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
Knees swollen and painful. Acute
articular rheumatism ; worse, touch and motion, pro-
luse sweat. Pain shifts. Sciatica, burning pain; worse
at night. Copious foot-sweat.

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
> — Itching vesicles and pustules ; better by
scratching. Sweat without sleep. Urticaria. Hot and
burning skin. Purpura. Herpes zoster.

sections.label: Relationship
sections.text:
Compare: Salol (rheumatic pain in
joints, with soreness and stiffness, headache over eyes;
urine violet-smelling) ; Colch,; China; Lact, ac.

Dose — Third decimal trituration.

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Vertigo, 3 .—Dulness of the head, 3 .—Rush of blood to the head, 3 .
—Headache, 3 .

Eye .—Diminished acuteness of vision, 3 .

Ear .— Diminished hearing, 3 .-[io.j Roaring in the ears, lasting six
hours (after two hours), 3 .— Roaring in the ears, with difficult hearing, 3 .

sections.label: Nose
sections.text: Sneezing, 3 .

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
Burning in the mouth and epigastric region, 3 .—Dryness and
burning in the mucous membrane of the mouth and pharynx, 3 .— Burning
and scraping in the mouth and throat, 3 .—Solutions stronger than 1 to 1000
are corrosive to the mucous membranes, and for the time being turn them
white, 3 .—Extremely disgusting taste, 3 .

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Scraping in the throat causing cough, 3 .—Burning in the
throat, 3 .—[20.] Haemorrhagic pharyngitis, with difficulty of swallowing, 3 .
—Great dryness of the pharynx, 3 .—Slight difficulty in swallowing (after
three hours) ; violent efforts to swallow, with difficulty in swallowing, woke
him from sleep (first night) ; the pain and difficulty in swallowing became
confined to the right side of the throat, with sticking paiu extending along
the Eustachian tube to within the ear; swelling of the right tonsil, so that
it was noticed externally below the angle of the jaw, with sensitiveness
when touched, and with increased temperature in the vicinity ; examina¬
tion revealed redness and swelling of the mucous membrane of the throat
and posterior fauces, with ulcers of the size of the head of a pin ; after a
time a small lump of cheesy matter of a strong odor was expectorated,
with some bluish-red blood ; this was followed by a gradual return of the
throat to its normal condition, 1 .

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Vomiting, 3 .—Very frequent vomiting, 3 . — Erosions and
ulcers in the stomach and bowels, 3 .—(In a case of acute miliary tubercu¬
losis, who died after taking 12 grams of the acid dissolved in alcohol, there
were found in the stomach half a dozen deep ulcers as large as peas, ap¬
parently caused by haemorrhagic erosions due to the irritating action of the
drug), 3 .—(Ecchymoses and ulcerations in the mucous membrane of the
stomach), 3 .—Burning in the epigastric region, 3 .

Urinary Oryans. —Three hours afterwards the urine which I passed
was of a green tinge, and small crystalline bodies in great numbers could
be seen in it on holding the bottle which contained it against the bright
light. On leaving the bottle for a few hours standing at rest, a copious
precipitate of a white feathery consistence was seen occupying the bottom
of the bottle to the extent of about half an inch ; this precipitate is Sali¬
cyluric acid. On microscopic examination it is found to consist of crystals
of one form, but presenting a different appearance as seen from various
points of view ; they are six-sided bodies, oblong in shape, of a fine silverv-
white color, and showing none of the reactions which uric acid gives with
the various chemical tests. If the crystals are filtered off the urine at
once becomes putrid, but if left alone will remain fresh for above a week, 2 .

Generalities. —[30.] Immediately after the first powder, he began
to sweat profusely. The perspiration increased and his strength dimin-

SALIX PURPUREA.

475

i?hed so visibly, that his wife was unwilling to give him the fourth powder.
He insisted, however, and after taking it, vomiting and an agonizing head¬
ache set in, which continued all night. In the morning he seemed uncon¬
scious, and simply groaned loudly. Only for a moment did his mind seem
clear, when he cried out, “ My head, my head!” to the physicians who were
present. All treatment was futile, and he died in forty hours after taking
the first powder. No post-mortem examination was permitted. The course
of the case was too rapid to be explained on the theory of a complicating
cerebral inflammation ; ail the symptoms seem to point to poisoning (10-
grain doses), 3 .

Fevev . —Increased warmth of the skin, 3 .—Profuse sweat, 3 .—Sweat, at
times more, at times less profuse, 3 .—Sweat, 3 .

SALIX PURPUREA.

Salix purpurea, Linn.

Natural order, Salicaceae.

Common names, Red or purple willow.

Preparation, Tincture of the hark.

Authorities. 1, Dr. T. C. Duncan, Trans. Horn. Med. Soc. State of N.
Y., 1870, p. 328, chewed the hark ; 1 a, same, took twice, a drachm of an
infusion ; 2, same, Mrs. D., took (for haemorrhoids) about a drachm of an
infusion.

Mi lid. —Very nervous and despondent, all day (second day), 1 *.—Nerv¬
ous and very irritable all day, until evening (third day), 2 .—Dulness of the
intellect (second day), 11 .

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
In a few minutes I felt a full dizzy feeling in the head, com¬
mencing just in front of the ears and passing up to the vertex, like a wave;
this giddy feeling lasted for a few minutes; I had to sit down and keep
quiet until it passed off (after first dose) ; the same, full, giddy feeling in
the head, hut in a less marked degree (second day), 1 * 2 .

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
It has a peculiar astringent taste, puckering the mucous
membrane of the buccal cavity and closing Steno’s duct, 1 .—Taste of undi¬
gested food (second day), 1 *.

'Throat. —Swelling of the right parotid gland (second day), 1 *.

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Flatulence (second day), 1 *.—Pain in the abdomen (second
day), 1 *.

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
[10.] Bowels loose; two stools to-day (second day), 1 *.—The
bowels moved twice, with gripings in the abdomen (third day), 2 .

Urinary Ore/ans .—Urine slightly acid ; excess of the triple and
earthy phosphates and epithelium ; less uric acid crystals (?) (second
day), 1 *.

Tacit. —Aching in the right acetabulum (second day), 1 *.

Heart and Pulse. —Circulation torpid (second day), 11 .—Pulse fee¬
ble (third day), 2 .

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Rested poorly, waked often ; first too hot, then chilly; and at
last, towards morning, in a profuse perspiration (first night), 1 *.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
First too hot, then chilly, and at last, towards morning, in a
profuse perspiration (first night), 1 *.

476

SAMBUCUS CANADENSIS.

SAMBUCUS CANADENSIS.

Sambucus canadensis, L.

Natural order, Caprifoliacese.

Common name, Elder.

Preparation, Tincture of the flowers.

Authority. (Dr. A. Uebelacker, Morristown, New Jersey, MS. to editor.)
1, Took tincture, 20 drops, first day ; 50 drops, second and third days ; la,
same, a week later, took tincture (of buds, flowers, tender shoots, and leaves),
20 drops, first, and 30 drops, third day.

sections.label: Mind
sections.text:
With the drawing in the head an unusual depression of spirits
was felt; an indefinable fear as if the horse (a very gentle animal) might
run away, or the wagon break at any moment; a dread of some undefined
danger (after one hour), 1 .

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Severe drawing in the head, with fulness; on motion it felt as
if water were undulating in it, with unusual depression of spirits (after one
hour), 1 .—The same drawing and fulness in the head, followed by sharp,
darting pains through the head (after half an hour, second day), 1 .—Head
felt heavy, confused, with drawing and darting pains (after one hour), 1 *.

sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Face flushed (after one hour), 1 .—The face was so flushed, that
a friend meeting me on the road, said: “Doctor, you’d better go home, you
are sick ; your face is all broken out in blotches, and you look bad ” (after
one hour, second day), 1 .

Moutll .—Mouth dry; felt so parched as to stop at a farmhouse and
ask for a drink (after one hour), 1 .

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Th roat and mucous lining of larynx and trachea felt dry
and swollen, impeding free respiration (second day), 1 *.

Urinary Organs. —Pressure in renal region, followed by frequent
and profuse flow of urine, looking clear (after two hours), 1 .—[10.] Fre¬
quent urination (after one hour, second day, and after one hour and a half,
third day), 1 .—The urine contained albumen (nitric acid test), 1 *.

Respiratory Organs. —Breathing labored, similar to asthma (after
two hours, first day, and after one hour, second day), 1 .—Respiration wheez¬
ing (second day), 1 *.—Had to sit up in bed to get breath (second day), 1 *.

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Unaccountable heaviness and constriction in the chest, as if a
heavy load were pressing on it; the heart began to labor heavily ; palpi¬
tation set in ; the sense of oppression made me gasp for breath at times;
breathing labored, similar to asthma (after two hours, first day, and after
one hour, second day), 1 .—Aroused from sleep by a terrible constriction of
chest and heart; had to jump up in bed to get my breath ; could not lie
down for fear of choking (after one hour and a half, third day), 1 .—Feeling
of soreness in chest and region of heart (third day), 1 *.

Heart and Pulse. —Sharp pain in the heart (in the region of the
valves), with palpitation, the heart at times working so hard as to be ob¬
served by the movement of the vest (after one hour), 1 ’.—Heart began to
labor heavily; palpitation set in (after two hours, first day, and after one
hour, second day), 1 .— [20.] Pulse rose to 100, but became normal at end
of perspiration (after three hours), 1 .

Pack. —Back felt sprained (after two hours), 1 .—Pain in back (after
one hour, second day), 1 .—Pressing pain in lumbar region (after two hours), 1 .
—Pressure in lumbar region (after one hour and a half, third day), 1 .

SAMBUCUS.

477

Extrem ities . —Sharp darting pains in hands and feet resemble rheu¬
matic pains (after one hour, second day), 1 .—Darting pains iu hands and feet
(after one hour and a half, third day), 1 .

Generalities. —Feeling of exhaustion, which remained during the
rest of the day (second day), 1 .—During all the provings a feeling of un¬
easiness, of unrest, was a very marked symptom, 11 .—All the other symp¬
toms recurred again, first and second days, la .—[30.] Symptoms relieved by
sweat (second day), 1 .

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Perspiration, soon becoming profuse, which gradually relieved
all other symptoms (after three hours), 1 .—Profuse sweat, with relief of all
symptoms, except a feeling of exhaustion (second day), 1 .—Profuse perspira¬
tion relieving all symptoms ; I noticed that the head perspired less than
the rest of the body (third day), 1 .

Conditions.— Amelioration.— (Sweat.), The symptoms.

SAMBUCUS.

Sambucus nigra, Linn.

Natural order, Caprifoliaceae.

Common names. Elder; (G.), Flieder,Schwarzer Holunder; (Fr.),Sureau.

Preparation, Tincture of the leaves and flowers.

Authorities. (Nos. 1 to 7 from Hahnemann, R. A. M. L., 5, 61.) 1,

Hahnemann ; 2, Franz; 3, Gross; 4. Hartmann ; 5, Laughammer; 6,
Wislicenus; 7, Haller, Arzneira, Leipzig, 1806, p. 349, effects of external
application ; 8. Lembke, A. H. Z., 49,179, proving with half a teaspoonful
of tincture; 9, Christison, Loud. Med. Gaz., 1830, 5, p. 824, effects of eat¬
ing the leaves and flowers, in a boy; 10, same, effects of eating the flowers
only in a boy.

ALind .— Periodical delirium, saw frightful things on the wall, 1 . —* Con¬
stant fretjulness; everything produces a disagreeable impression, 5 .

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
VertiiJO. Dizzy in the morning, on rising, 1 .—Dizziness, ob¬
scuration of the head, lasting a few minutes (after one hour), 2 .—Dizziness
on moving the head, with a tensive sensation as if water were in it (after
twenty-four hours), 2 .—Very giddy on rising, in the morning; in the forenoon
the giddiness increased so much that he staggered iu walking, like a drunken
man (second day), 10 . —General Head. Violent headache (first night), 10 .
—Pressure from within outward to all sides of the head,*.—Pressive stupe¬
fying headache, as in catarrh, 5 .—[10.] Pressive stupefying headache, as
from intoxication (after twenty hours), 5 . — Forehead. Pressive headache
in the forehead and a sudden painful jerk through the brain, from one side
to the other (after a quarter of an hour), 6 .—Tearing pressive headache in the
upper part of the forehead, with paius streaming down iuto the eye (after
two days), 2 .— Temples , Pressive tearing headache over the left temple,
in the bone, on stooping, 2 .—Pressure outwards in the temples (after one
hour), 6 .—Very transient intermittent tearing in the temples, more in the
bone (after ten hours), 2 . — Vertex and Occiput. Burrowing headache
in the vertex (after a quarter of an hour), 6 .—Tearing stitch through the left
half of the occiput, frequently returning and lasting a long time, with a dull
sensation in the same place, during the intervals (after half an hour),*.—
External Head. Itching on the forehead relieved by rubbing (after
a quarter of an hour), 6 .

478

SAMBUCUS.

Eye. —Pupils at first contracted, and after forty to forty-four hours
greatly dilated, 5 .

Ear. — [20.] Sharp stitches within the right ear, together with cramp¬
like pain (after a quarter of an hour), 6 .—Itching and crawling in the ears
and throat; in the throat somewhat relieved by the tongue, 1 .

sections.label: Nose
sections.text:
A pressing forward and a sensation of heaviness in the tip of
the nose; as if it would bleed (after two days), 2 .

sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Face flushed (third day), 9 .—Sensation of warmth, like flushing,
mounting into the face (after one hour and a half), 2 .—Tensive pain, as
from swelling of the cheek, with numbness (after eleven hours), 2 .—Tension
in the left cheek, with gnawing pressure upon the superior maxillary bone, 2 .

Month. —Tearing and stitches in the left upper and lower teeth, ex¬
tending forward into the incisors (after two hours); the pain then extended
to the eye, with a sensation as if the cheek were swollen, which was not the
case, 1 .—Great dryness of the palate, without thirst, 2 .—Soreness of the mouth
and throat (second day), 9 .

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
[30.] Thirst, though drink has not a pleasant taste, 1 .—Oc¬
casional hiccough (third day), 9 .—Hiccough, during and after eating, 2 .—
Sensation of commencing nausea in and below the pit of the stomach, 3 .—
* Vomiting occurred frequently in the course of the day, and towards even¬
ing was tinged with blood (third day), 9 .—Feeling of dull pressure in the
epigastric region (after four hours), 3 .—Small stitches just below the stom¬
ach, aggravated by pressure (while sitting), (after a quarter of an hour), 4 .

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Rumbling in the abdomen, 3 .—Fine griping in the right
abdominal muscles, below the short ribs (after one hour), 6 .—Fine tearing in
the leftside of the abdomen (after one hour), 6 .—[40.] Excessive tenderness
over the whole belly (first day); the tenderness became so great that he could
not allow it to be touched (second day) ; tense, much swelled, and exceed¬
ingly tender (third day), 9 .—Severe griping (first day); the tormina recurred
with violence every half hour (second day), 9 .— Griping in the abdomen,
with emission of flatus, as after taking cold (after forty-eight hours), 5 .—Grip¬
ing pain in the abdomen, if it leans against a sharp corner, 2 .—The abdomen
is sore internally, the intestines feel bruised, 2 .—Pressure in the abdomen,
with nausea, as soon as it presses against anything (after ten hours and a
half), 2 .—Stitches in the left side of the abdominal muscles, descending ob¬
liquely, while sitting and standing (after four hours), 2 .—Sticking in the
left side of the lower abdomen, over the hip, rather dull and needlelike
stitches, rhythmical-like pulsations, lasting a quarter of an hour, increasing
and decreasing, 3 .—Spasmodic tearing in the abdominal muscles, especially
on moving them, in the evening after lying down (after twelve hours), 6 .

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
Very thin slimy stool, with much flatus, followed immediately
bv renewed urging; distension of abdomen, with pressure in the stomach
and umbilical region. A second stool later, but afterwards no further
symptoms. 8 .

Urinary Organs. —[50.] Itching in the orifice of the urethra
(after one hour), 6 .—The urine passes in a thin stream (after ten hours), 2 .—
Frequent desire to urinate, with scanty discharge (after two and eighteen
hours), 5 .—^Frequent desire to urinate, with much discharge (after thirty-
eight hours), 5 .—Obliged to urinate at night, 3 .—Frequent micturition of
dark-yellow urine, 4 .

Sexual Organs. —Emission after midnight, 2 .

Respiratory Organs.— -"Hoarseness caused by much tenacious
glutinous mucus in the larynx, 2 .

SAMBUCUS.

479

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
* Oppression and pressure beneath the sternum, and pressure in
the pit of the stomach and epigastric region, with nausea and sense of weakness
(after five hours), 2 .—* Oppression and stitches in the left side of the chest,
below the nipple (after five hours), 2 .—[60.] Cuttiug gripiug iu the last false
ribs, extending to the spine (after nine hours), 6 .—Sharp intermittent cutting
in front, on the third false rib, especially on moving the trunk (after three
hours), 6 .—Sudden internal clawing iu both sides of the chest, about the
fourth true rib (after half an hour), 6 .

Pulse. —Pulse more rapid, somewhat above 70 (after two hours), 3 .—
The pulse becomes slower, and falls from 70 to 60 (after half an hour), 3 .—
Pulse 10 beats slower, but fuller (after six hours),' 2 .—Pulse frequent and
small (third day), 9 .

JSeck and Back .—Pressive heaviness in the nape of the neck, mak¬
ing it more difficult than usual to move the head (after half an hour), 6 .—
Cutting stitches deep in the cervical muscles on both sides, especially on
moving the neck (after half an hour), 6 .—Pressive pain iu the middle of the
spine, not relieved by any motion, lasting a long time (after half an hour), 4 .
—[70.] Pulsating throbbing sticking beneath the right scapula, while sit¬
ting, 2 .—Cutting stitches in the scapulse, during rest (after a quarter of an
hour), 6 .—Sharp stitches in the inner surface of the right scapula, extending
from within outward, during rest, 6 .—Drawing pressure in the small of the
back, extending forward into the ilium internally, in the muscles, while
standing (after two hours), 2 .—Cutting thrusts iu the sacrum, most violent
on bending forward, with pain like a tension (after nine hours), 6 .

Superior Ext realities. —Fine pinching in the axilla (after a
quarter of an hour), 6 .—As soon as he supports himself on the upper arm
it seems as though it would break (after three hours), 2 .—Fine stitches in
the middle of the inner side of the upper arm (after one hour), 6 .—Paralytic
heaviness iu the elbow-joints (after half an hour), 6 .—In both wrists cutting
stitches rhythmical with the pulse, somewhat relieved by motion (after a
quarter of an hour), 6 .—[80.] Drawing pain iu the bones of the wrist and
along the radius, during rest, 2 .—Sharp stitches iu the outer condyle of the
wrist (after half au hour), 6 .—Trembling of the hands, while writing, 2 .—
Tearing iu the finger-joints, 1 .—Crawling iu the fingers, that are very cold
(after half an hour), 6 .

Inferior Extremities. —Tearing pain around above the hip-joint,
only on walking (after three-quarters of an hour), 4 .—Sticking itching on
the inner sides of both thighs, that after rubbing changes to burning (after
one hour), 6 .—A drawing-sticking sensation through the anterior muscles of-
the upper part of the right thigh, during rest (after three hours and a
half), 4 .—Cramplike drawing on the posterior and upper portion of the
thigh, at the insertion of the large gluteal muscle, while walking, 2 .—The
hamstrings are very tense and seem too short, so that standing is difficult
(after four hours aud a half), 2 .—[90.] Sensation of weariness in the legs,
with a feeling as if cold air were blowing upou them; both felt only while
standing (after half au hour), 4 .—Sensation of deaduess, as if asleep, and
coldness, in the middle of the right tibia, while standing (after four hours), 2 .
—Sharp deeply-piercing stitches on the inner side of the tibia, somewhat
relieved by motion (after half an hour), 6 .—Tearing paiu iu the right ex¬
ternal malleolus and in the muscles on the side of the leg, iu the evening,
in bed, 2 .

Generalities. —* Dropsical swellings? f—* Great tendency to start; he

f From the external application.

starts at things to which he is constantly accustomed,' 1 . Orgasm of blood, in
the evening, half an hour after lying down, with a sensation of trembling, 1 .
—* Most of the pains occur during rest and disappear during motion; only a
few are caused by motion,' 1 .

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
Red spots here and there on the cheeks, with a burning sensa¬
tion (after one hour), 1 .—A painless suppurating pimple, with red areola,
on the left side of the lower lip (after thirty-seven hours), 5 .—[100.] Sud¬
den painful drawing in all points over the surface of the body, while sitting
(after three hours), 2 .—Itching on the back of the nose, with a slight sen¬
sation of numbness of the skin (after three hours and a half), 2 .—Violent
itching on the patella, with a raw scraping sensation ; a sensation as if an
eruption would break out (after four hours and a half), 2 .

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
* Sleepiness , without sleep, 1 .—Starting out of sleep, at night,
with anxiety and shortness of breath, even to suffocation, and with trem¬
bling, 1 .—Slumber with half-opened eyes and mouth; on waking, could not
catch his breath; was obliged to sit up, and then the breath was very rapid,
with whistling in the chest, as though he would suffocate; he beat about
with his hands; the head and hands were bluish and puffy; he was hoarse,
without thirst; when the attacks came on he cried; all this happened with¬
out cough, and especially at night, from 12 to 4, 1 .f—Frequent waking from
sleep, as from wakefulness, 5 .—Restless sleep; on sitting up in bed it seemed
as though the symptoms extended downward and she felt easier, 1 .—Dreams
at night, 1 .—Lascivious dream, with emission, 5 . -[ 110 .] Vivid unremem¬
bered dreams, 11 .

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chilliness. Shivering over the whole body, with fine stick¬
ing crawling here and there, especially with very cold hands and feet;
shivering especially extending from the feet to the knees (after a quarter
of an hour), 6 .—Coldness creeps over the whole body, especially on the hands
and feet, which are cold to touch, though the latter may be warmly wrapped
up (after half an hour), 4 .—Repeated attacks of slight shivering (after half
an hour), 3 .—Shaking chill before going to bed (after four hours), 1 .—Slight
chilliness, though the face was warmer than usual (after one hour), 3 .—
Hands very cold (after one hour), 3 .—Icy-cold feet, though the body was
otherwise warm (after three-quarters of an hour), 4 .— Iieflt. Plot and fever¬
ish (first day), 9 .—Violent general heat while walking (after three hours), 6 .
— [120.] Decided heat is noticed on touch, especially in the palms of the
hands and soles of the feet, 1 .—Intolerable sensation of dry heat over the
whole body, 1 .—* During the heat dread of uncovering; it seemed as though
he would take cold or be attacked with colic, 1 .—Heat over the whole body,
without thirst, soon after lying down (after two hours), 1 .—Sensation of
warmth in the head and throat; even to touch the face and other parts of
the body were warmer than usual, though without thirst, 3 . — Frequent
flushes of heat, with great heat of the face, and after half an hour sweat
broke out upon the face, in the afternoon (after ten hours), 2 .—* Sensation
of burning heat in the face, with moderate warmth of the body and icy coldness
of the feet, without thirst (after one hour), 4 .— Sweat. *Profu.se sweat,
without thirst, while awake, from 7 p.m. to 1 a.m. ; drops stood upon the
face, and there was also perspiration all over, but after sleep he was more hot
than sweaty, but without thirst, 1 . —Rather profuse sweat after midnight, but
not on the head, 3 .— *He was sweaty all over on leaking from sleep, two

f A kind of Millar’s asthma.

SAN GUINARI A.

481

nights, 5 . —[130.] Sweat first on the face, occurring several hours after the
dry heat had disappeared, 1 .

Conditions. — Aggravation. — (Morning), On rising, dizzy.— ( Moving
head), Dizziness.— (Moving neck), Stitches in cervical muscles.— (Pressure),
Stitches below stomach.— (During rest), Pain in bones of wrist and along
radius; most pains.—( While sitting), Sticking beneath right scapula.—
( While standing), Pressure in small of back ; weariness and feeling of cold¬
ness in legs.— (On walking), Pain around hip-joint; general heat.

Amelioration. — (During motion), Most pains.
